solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enough space for sentimentality to explode?

parts.note: mush is soppy, sentimental stuff
room is space, as in 'room enough'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there is room for all the soppiness before it bursts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enough space for sentimentality' is room for mush, which put the other way round gives the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring up or grow suddenly and dramatically, like a fungus overnight, is a figurative sense of this verb.

clue.text: Swine and Circe's end added to Homer, possibly

parts.note: a swine is a pig

indicators.note: the end of the word is its final letter

parts.note: on means added to, as in 'tacked on'

explanation.surface: In the Odyssey, Circe turned men into swine; the clue plays on Homer the poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer looks like the Greek poet, matching Circe, but a homer is a homing bird. 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing bird trained to fly back to its loft, one kind of this bird.

clue.text: Anorak's success with music presenter topped hit repeatedly

parts.note: a win is a success
a DJ (disc jockey) presents music

indicators.note: with its top taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to hammer is to strike again and again

explanation.surface: An anorak (a nerdy enthusiast) triumphs with a disc jockey who has been pounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anorak' reads as the nerdy enthusiast, but it is the garment. 'topped' removes the H of HAMMER, leaving AMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A windproof jacket is called by this name, as is an anorak, a hooded weatherproof coat.

clue.text: Like so many a bully, elbowing geek's head

indicators.note: elbowing pushes someone out of the way, so the letter is removed

parts.note: bullies in number are thugs

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gang of bullies shoves aside a nerd, as many do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elbowing' pushes the G (geek's head) out of THUGS.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in this way or manner, which is what 'like so' says.

clue.text: Maths ace's complicated diagrams

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, leaving ace

explanation.surface: A brilliant mathematician's diagrams are hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges MATHS and ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemata is the plural of schema, an outline plan or diagrammatic representation.

clue.text: One refusing to face facts bridled when getting comeuppance?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word coming up is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a horse bridled is reined in

explanation.surface: Someone in denial bristled when they finally got what was coming to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeuppance' is split as come-up: REINED read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who denies what is true or undeniable is one who refuses to face facts.

clue.text: Imprisoned in short month, top-rank detectives get backing from the bench

indicators.note: being imprisoned in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: Jul is the short form of July

indicators.note: backing means the words are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detectives

explanation.surface: Senior detectives jailed for a short spell win support from judges.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is read as AI. 'get backing' turns A1 CID into DICIA, which is 'Imprisoned in' JUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from the bench means coming from judges or a court, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Half in Lima (the rest cast off coat) copy fashion

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word is its first two letters
the rest of Lima, its last two letters, is taken off the coat

parts.note: a mackintosh is a raincoat
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Someone copies a style while wearing half a coat in Peru's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of Lima gives LI; 'the rest cast off' means the other half, MA, is removed from MACKINTOSH, giving CKINTOSH.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something proper form by working on it is to fashion it, an idiom from bear cubs supposedly licked into form.

clue.text: Poor journo and his boss like a lot of voicemail

parts.note: a hack is a mediocre journalist
ED is short for editor, a journalist's boss

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist and his editor, like those of the UK phone-hacking scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK phone-hacking scandal, tabloid reporters broke into people's voicemail.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages broken into by intruders were described this way during the phone-hacking affair at British tabloids.

clue.text: Stroppy woman finally regretted showing cunning

parts.note: a shrew is a bad-tempered, nagging woman

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered woman eventually regrets showing her craftiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astute and sharp in judgement is close to being cunning; the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Superficial quote marks Socialist in U-turn

indicators.note: a U-turn sends the sequence back the other way

parts.note: to quote is to cite
M is an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A shallow party quotation shows a Socialist doing a policy reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in U-turn' reverses the whole string CITE M SOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only skin-deep, for appearance rather than substance, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: One unseen in simulation of silken audio?

definitions.text: One unseen in simulation of silken audio?

indicators.note: a simulation is an imitation, so the letters are remade into a different arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, which goes 'unseen' from the mix

explanation.surface: An impersonator copies a smooth voice so well that nobody sees the difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unseen' means I (One) is missing: SILKEN AUDIO without an I is rearranged. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation that sounds like the original, unseen but heard, is what this noun names.

clue.text: Craggy priest died in deplorable side of Celtic festival

indicators.note: one piece goes in another
deplorable suggests a sorry mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: Father Ted is the priest of Craggy Island in the Irish TV sitcom Father Ted

explanation.surface: A rugged-faced priest dies, sadly, at a Celtic festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craggy' looks like a description of the priest, but it points to Father Ted of Craggy Island in the Irish sitcom. TED D goes 'in' EISFOD, made by 'deplorable' from SIDE OF.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh national festival of music and poetry competitions goes by this name, a Celtic cultural gathering.

clue.text: Beauty marries Beast: their hearts glow

indicators.note: the hearts of the three words are their central letters

explanation.surface: In the fairy tale, Beauty weds the Beast and their hearts shine with love.
explanation.walkthrough: The centres are AU from Beauty, R from marries and A from Beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive radiance or atmosphere surrounding a person is a glow in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Vexed at museum's Dada, her sculpture attempted realism

indicators.note: vexed means troubled or agitated, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: here the 's supplies an S, giving museums

explanation.surface: A realist sculptor is annoyed at a gallery's Dada exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vexed' rearranges AT MUSEUMS DADA. Dada was an anti-realist art movement, a neat contrast with her lifelike waxworks.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-born wax modeller founded the London waxworks famed for lifelike figures of the famous.

clue.text: Hesitant person needs one comforting word when doctor comes round

indicators.note: the doctor's letters surround the rest

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
'there, there' is said to soothe

explanation.surface: An indecisive patient needs reassurance when the doctor visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wavers and cannot make up their mind is a hesitant person.

clue.text: Noise ultimately produced in resonant metal object

definitions.text: Noise ultimately produced in resonant metal object

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: one letter goes in the other piece

parts.note: a gong is a resonating metal disc

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

explanation.surface: The racket that a struck gong finally makes.
explanation.walkthrough: The D from 'produced' goes 'in' GONG after its first letter. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound of a bell, or by extension a noisy row, is described by this echoic word.

clue.text: Funny scene in second gear

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A comic moment happens while the car is in second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second gear' reads as a car's gear but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch is a funny scene in a revue or show.

clue.text: Getting a thousand for half as much, lower penalties will come my way

indicators.note: getting one thing in place of another means a swap
for means in exchange for

parts.note: deeper means lower down
D is the Roman numeral for 500, half of M, which is a thousand
K is the abbreviation for a thousand

explanation.surface: A goalie pondering being paid more while the penalty count rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap puts K (a thousand) in place of D (500, half of M) in DEEPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper faces penalty kicks, so a goalie could say that shots from the spot are aimed at them.

clue.text: Uncovered fresh marmalade ingredient with gallons about

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: pectin is the setting agent in jam and marmalade

explanation.surface: A cook's note about fresh marmalade and how many gallons are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' strips F and H from FRESH, leaving RES.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means concerning or with regard to, a synonym for about.

clue.text: Combat vehicle advanced to get loaded

parts.note: a tank is an armoured combat vehicle
up means advanced or ahead, as in 'two goals up'

explanation.surface: An armoured vehicle moves forward to have ammunition put aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' reads as ammunition, but here it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting drunk is informally getting loaded; this phrasal verb means to drink heavily.

clue.text: Prepared for conflict over eating date sugar

indicators.note: the reversed word eats, enclosing, the other piece
over means turned over, read the other way

parts.note: armed means ready for war
an era is a date or period in history

explanation.surface: Troops ready for battle eating a date with sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' gives DEMRA. 'date' reads as the fruit, apt beside sugar, but here it is a period in history.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a type of light brown cane sugar, named after a region of Guyana.

clue.text: Alternative for porter with cross to bear, in need of wheeled cart?

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the beer holds the cross

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, and ale is another beer one might have instead
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A station porter with a heavy load needs a trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' suggests a baggage carrier, but it is the beer. The definition is a playful description: a wheeled cart needs one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod on which wheels turn is what any wheeled cart needs, so the question-marked phrase hints at it.

clue.text: Expose study due for revision

parts.note: a den is a study or private room

indicators.note: revision suggests the letters are rewritten in another order

explanation.surface: Revision time reveals how much studying was done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for revision' rearranges DUE into UDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip bare or lay open something is to expose it; the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps give another ring to cancel

definitions.meaning: split as ..., to sound the bells again
to revoke a law is to cancel it

explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the word means revoke a law; split, it means peal the bells a second time.

clue.text: Persuasive European group keeping ruler apart from English

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

indicators.note: apart from means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a queen is a ruler

explanation.surface: A persuasive European bloc holds a monarch but not the English one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from English' takes one E out of QUEEN, leaving QUEN, which LOT is 'keeping'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent and expressive speech that moves listeners is persuasive; the adjective is a near synonym.
